defects_found.finding: EnterWorktree derives its own branch name (worktree-aidlc+<id>); the orchestrator renamed the branch mid-session to match the documented aidlc/<id> convention.
defects_found.fix: Orchestrator now accepts the host branch name and never renames; git worktree add is the fallback only.

defects_found.finding: The orchestrator passed the change ID plus prose as Skill arguments, so a stage skill rendered "Change ID: trial-ce-brainstorm — feature request: ..." against its own one-ID contract.
defects_found.fix: Orchestrator must pass the bare change ID and state context as conversation text.

defects_found.finding: With CE absent, aidlc-intent ran find / -maxdepth 4 -iname "*compound-engineering*" to hunt for the plugin — the out-of-scope filesystem discovery previously recorded as a defect.
defects_found.fix: aidlc-intent now decides availability from the session skill catalog alone; filesystem/plugin-cache hunting is forbidden.

defects_found.finding: A project-scope declaration (extraKnownMarketplaces + enabledPlugins) did not install CE in a fresh clone: 0 CE skills with project,local and with user,project,local, before and after the interactive trust prompt; 35 after claude plugin install --scope project. The source repo where install had run reported 35.
defects_found.fix: README and USAGE now state the declaration pins the marketplace/plugin but each engineer installs once per clone.

also_observed.user_scope_interference: With user settings enabled, a user-scope task-observer skill auto-fired and probed ~/.claude/skill-observations, and aidlc* command count rose from 13 to 20 because a user-scope plugin ships its own aidlc skills.

limits: Only intent was run; design through review, /aidlc-fix and /aidlc-learn were not exercised in this session.
CE took its fast path, so scan/scout, Path B artifacts and CONCEPTS.md maintenance were not exercised.
The trial ran in a disposable clone with a broad local allowlist; it is not evidence about permission behaviour under stricter policy.
Gate answers were driven through a PTY; no real product-owner participated.
